q-7527: Correct answer: C. Carrying people in a trailer towed by a lorry is prohibited, because there are no seats, belts or protection in a collision there. The exception concerns solely the vehicles of certain services, for example the Police.
q-7529: Correct answer: B. Outside the driver's cab, people may be carried only in seats. Riding standing is not permitted, and placing people between the load and the cab risks crushing when the load shifts under braking.
q-7531: Correct answer: B. Long timber carried on a stanchion trailer may protrude at the rear by at most 5 m. The protruding end must be marked, because other drivers misjudge the real length of the combination, especially when overtaking and at junctions.
q-7532: Correct answer: A. A load protruding beyond the vehicle's outline is always marked, without any threshold length. The driver cannot see such a protrusion from their seat, and other road users must notice it early enough.
q-7533: Correct answer: B. A load protruding in front of the vehicle is marked with an orange flag, clearly visible in daylight. Neither yellow nor red is provided for this, and after dusk the protruding part must additionally be lit.
q-7534: Correct answer: C. The driver of a vehicle carrying people outside the cab may neither eat nor smoke while driving. They must be in full control of the vehicle and drive smoothly, because those carried are not protected like passengers in the cab.
q-7538: Correct answer: B. A bus driver may not eat while driving when carrying other people. When nobody is in the vehicle the ban does not apply, but eating still must not distract from driving.
q-7539: Correct answer: B. A bus with a trailer coupled to it may not be towed — such a combination would be excessively long and hard to control. The trailer must be uncoupled and towed separately.
q-7540: Correct answer: C. Towing a vehicle with a trailer attached is prohibited regardless of the type of road. A three-part combination would be too long and unstable, so the trailer must be uncoupled and moved separately.
q-7542: Correct answer: C. In the trailer of a tourist road train people are carried only in seats. A standing passenger easily loses balance under braking or on a bend and may fall out of the trailer.
q-7602: Correct answer: C. An agricultural tractor is marked at the rear with the triangular plate distinguishing a slow-moving vehicle, set point upwards. Triangular reflectors are reserved for trailers, so a tractor without a trailer does not use them.
q-7603: Correct answer: B. The tyres on the wheels of one axle must be of the same type and have the same tread, because different grip on the wheels of the same axle pulls the combination sideways and causes loss of stability under braking. The other answers give requirements that the rules do not impose.
q-7607: Correct answer: A. The trailer blocks the view through the rear window, and the mirrors show only the sides of the combination, so both sources of the picture must be used at the same time. With limited visibility the driver should additionally get the help of another person.
q-7613: Correct answer: A. The trailer cuts the curve and runs closer to the inner edge than the tractor, so the bend must be taken wider. Otherwise its wheels catch the kerb, the verge or an obstacle standing on the inside of the bend.
q-7615: Correct answer: B. The payload given by the manufacturer is a limit value, following from the strength of the trailer's frame, axle, tyres and brakes. Exceeding it lengthens the braking distance and risks a failure, so the rules allow no tolerance here.
q-7617: Correct answer: A. A load protruding more than 0.5 m beyond the rear of the vehicle's outline must be marked, so that those behind can judge the real length of the combination. The marking must be clearly visible after dusk and in conditions of reduced clarity of the air as well.
q-7663: Correct answer: B. The number of people carried may not exceed the number of seats entered in the registration document, because it follows from the vehicle's design and its permissible mass. An overloaded bus takes longer to brake and loses stability.
q-7664: Correct answer: B. The stop brake immobilises the bus while passengers get on and off, so that the vehicle does not move with the doors open. The service brake serves for emergency braking, and the parking brake for a longer stop.
q-7688: Correct answer: A. A bus driver may not eat while carrying passengers — it occupies the hands and draws attention away from the road. A conversation on a hands-free kit and listening to the radio are not prohibited in themselves.
q-7725: Correct answer: C. A load may not protrude at the front more than 0.5 m beyond the front plane of the vehicle's outline, nor more than 1.5 m from the driver's seat. A load extending further limits the field of vision and makes judging dimensions harder.
q-7746: Correct answer: A. The load's centre of gravity is placed as close as possible to the vehicle's longitudinal axis, so that the wheels are loaded evenly and the vehicle is stable. Heavier items are placed low, and the method of fastening is matched to the load's properties.
q-7748: Correct answer: B. A high centre of gravity makes the load prone to tipping over in bends and under braking, so it often requires additional straps, braces or supports. A low centre of gravity does not release you from the duty to fasten it.
q-7771: Correct answer: C. First the passengers are taken to a safe place, because fire and smoke spread very quickly in a bus. Fighting the fire is attempted only after the evacuation and only when it does not endanger the rescuer.
q-8801: Correct answer: A. A child taller than 150 cm is carried like an adult passenger, that is, in a seat with the seat belt fastened, without a child seat. The duty to use a restraint concerns children shorter than 150 cm.
q-10794: Correct answer: A. With an actual total mass above 80 tonnes the journey requires piloting by two pilot vehicles — one in front of the combination, the other behind it. This duty covers the whole route, regardless of the time of day.
q-10797: Correct answer: A. Exceeding an actual total mass of 60 tonnes gives rise to a duty to pilot the journey. The pilot warns other drivers and leads the combination through difficult places, and the duty is not limited to night hours.
q-10807: Correct answer: A. Carrying a child rear-facing on the front seat is permitted only with the airbag switched off. The airbag deploys at great speed and would strike the back of the restraint, endangering the child's life.
q-10810: Correct answer: A. The threshold is a height of 150 cm: a shorter child must travel in a child seat or another restraint, on the front seat too. A taller child may use the seat belts alone, and age is of no significance here.
q-10812: Correct answer: A. A child seat is matched to the child's weight and height, and in addition must meet the technical conditions laid down in EU rules, which is confirmed by the approval mark on the label. The child's age alone is not a criterion here.
q-10813: Correct answer: B. When two child seats occupy the rear seat and a third physically does not fit, a third child may be carried on the rear seat in the seat belts alone, provided it is at least 3 years old.
q-10814: Correct answer: A. The exception concerns a child at least 135 cm tall for whom, because of height and weight, no suitable child seat can be found — it then travels on the rear seat secured with the seat belts alone.
q-10969: Correct answer: B. A child at least 135 cm tall, secured with the seat belts alone, may be carried only on the rear seat of the vehicle. Carrying such a child on the front seat without a restraint is not allowed.
q-11427: Correct answer: B. Burning fuel in a tanker risks a sudden flare-up and explosion, and a hand-held extinguisher is useless against such a fire. Move away to a safe distance, warn others and call the fire brigade.
q-11428: Correct answer: C. The incident is reported on the emergency number 112 or directly to the fire brigade on 998. The dispatcher must be told the location, the type of vehicle, the markings on the tanker and the number of casualties.
q-11436: Correct answer: B. A load may not protrude in front of the vehicle further than 1.5 m measured from the driver's seat. A longer overhang limits the field of vision and makes it harder to judge distance during manoeuvres.
q-11438: Correct answer: C. A vehicle together with its load may not exceed 4 m in height. Regardless of this, remember flyovers and tunnels where a sign gives a lower permitted value.
q-11440: Correct answer: A. The limiter in a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t is set to 90 km/h. This does not release the driver from observing the lower limits in force on the road in question.
q-11442: Correct answer: B. A lorry carrying people outside the driver's cab must be equipped with two fire extinguishers. They are placed so as to be easily accessible and kept in a condition fit for immediate use.
q-11443: Correct answer: C. The permitted height of a vehicle with its load is 4 m, so a combination measuring 4.5 m may not travel on any road. The type of road changes nothing here — the load must be reloaded or lowered.
q-11444: Correct answer: C. A load may not protrude sideways further than 23 cm from the plane of the vehicle's outline, so it must be arranged symmetrically. A greater overhang requires a permit for the journey of an oversize vehicle.
q-11445: Correct answer: B. The load on a single non-driven axle may not exceed 10 tonnes. On particular roads the permitted load is sometimes lower, as signs inform, and exceeding it requires a permit.
q-11474: Correct answer: C. The payload specified by the manufacturer is a design limit and may not be exceeded in any way. An overloaded vehicle brakes and handles worse, and its components and the road surface wear out faster.
q-11475: Correct answer: C. The basic condition is that the load must not impair the vehicle's stability or hinder steering. It is distributed evenly and as low as possible, secured against shifting, and so that it does not cover the lights and plates.
q-11476: Correct answer: C. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with a red-and-white striped panel with an area of at least 1,000 cm², placed at its end. After dusk a red light and a reflective element are added.
q-11477: Correct answer: C. Exceeding the permitted width makes the combination an oversize vehicle, which may travel only once a permit has been obtained. The permit specifies the route and the conditions of the journey, for example marking and piloting.
q-11480: Correct answer: A. A high or asymmetric centre of gravity increases the vehicle's tendency to lean when turning, braking and in a crosswind. The load is therefore arranged low and evenly on both sides.
q-11482: Correct answer: C. Liquid in a partly filled tank sloshes freely and, under braking and on a bend, strikes the tanker's wall with its mass, changing the distribution of the load. That is why you drive smoothly, with a margin of speed and distance.
q-11486: Correct answer: B. The journey of a vehicle heavier than a given stretch of road allows requires a permit, in which the route and the conditions of carriage are specified. No fee paid on your own initiative replaces such a permit.
q-11487: Correct answer: A. Exceeding the permitted height requires a permit for the journey of an oversize vehicle, in which a route is set that avoids flyovers, tunnels and overhead lines that are too low. Without such a document, driving is prohibited.
q-11488: Correct answer: B. Harsh braking may shift or loosen the load, so before driving on the driver checks its fastening and arrangement. The criterion is an event that may have disturbed the fastening, not the distance covered as such.
q-11516: Correct answer: A. Before setting off, the driver checks that the load is correctly arranged and fastened, so that it does not shift, fall off or impair the vehicle's stability. The check is always compulsory, not only when doubts arise.
q-11517: Correct answer: B. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with a clearly visible red-and-white striped geometric shape with a total area of no less than 1,000 cm². A white flag or a steady orange light does not serve for this marking.
q-11518: Correct answer: A. A load protruding more than 0.5 m at the rear is marked with red-and-white stripes with a total area of at least 1,000 cm², placed directly on the load. Black-and-yellow and black-and-white colours are not correct in this case.
q-11519: Correct answer: C. The actual total mass of a trailer towed by a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not exceed the actual total mass of that lorry plus 40%. Too heavy a trailer pushes the towing vehicle and lengthens the braking distance.
q-11527: Correct answer: A. On a descent speed is held with engine braking in a suitably low gear and with the retarder, and the service brake stays in reserve. Continuous braking with it overheats the system and reduces its effectiveness, and neutral deprives the vehicle of controlled slowing.
q-12478: Correct answer: A. Carrying in a bus more people than entered in the registration document by more than five results in the driving licence being retained for 3 months. The exception is public transport buses with standing places provided for.
q-13041: Correct answer: B. When carrying a child under seven in a motorcycle's sidecar, you may not ride faster than 40 km/h. This restriction applies regardless of the higher value the signs on the stretch permit.
q-13044: Correct answer: B. On this road the minimum distance in metres is half the numerical value of the speed in km/h. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h, which gives 40 m.
q-13050: Correct answer: B. When carrying a child under seven in a light quadricycle, you may not drive faster than 40 km/h. The general limit of 50 km/h in a built-up area does not apply here, because the lower value is binding.
q-6545: Correct answer: B. The situation behind is checked continuously in the mirrors, even when no manoeuvre is being carried out — on a motorway vehicles close in very fast. Turning the head at high speed takes the eyes off the road ahead of the motorcycle.
q-6748: Correct answer: B. On a motorway a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h. The higher speeds allowed on a motorway concern cars and light vehicles.
q-6787: Correct answer: B. A grip at 9 and 3 o'clock gives the surest control of the steering wheel and lets you carry out a sudden evasive manoeuvre without changing your hold. Hands at the top or bottom of the wheel are unstable and delay reaction at high speed.
q-6848: Correct answer: A. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules may travel on a motorway at up to 100 km/h. Other buses are bound there by the lower limit of 80 km/h.
q-6852: Correct answer: C. On a motorway a bus may travel at 80 km/h, and the number of seats does not change that. Faster, up to 100 km/h, may be driven only by buses meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules.
q-8812: Correct answer: B. On a motorway a rest is planned only in places intended for it, that is, at a service area. The hard shoulder and the exit slip road serve only for emergencies, and stopping on them risks being run into by another vehicle.
q-8852: Correct answer: B. A bus stops for a rest only at a service area, adapted for parked vehicles and the presence of passengers. The hard shoulder and the exit slip road are reserved for emergencies, and stopping on them risks being run into.
q-13057: Correct answer: C. Organised columns of motorcycles travelling on a motorway must be at least 500 m apart. Such a gap lets other drivers overtake safely and change lane between the groups.
q-13059: Correct answer: A. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions laid down in the rules may travel on a motorway at up to 100 km/h. A bus that does not meet those conditions is bound by a lower speed limit.
